html:
Brazil declared its independence from Portugal on 7 September 1822, when Prince Pedro, son of the Portuguese king, proclaimed it by the Ipiranga stream near São Paulo. He became Emperor Pedro I.

The Portuguese court had fled to Rio de Janeiro in 1808, during Napoleon's invasion, and Brazil became a kingdom equal to Portugal. When King João VI returned to Lisbon in 1821, the Portuguese parliament tried to reduce Brazil to a colony again. Pedro, left as regent, refused to return and broke with Portugal.

There was fighting in Bahia and the north, but the new empire held together, unlike Spanish America, which split into many republics. Portugal recognised independence in 1825. Brazil kept slavery and a monarchy until 1888 and 1889, under Pedro II.
sum: Brazil declared its independence from Portugal on 7 September 1822, when Prince Pedro, son of the Portuguese king, proclaimed it by the Ipiranga stream near São Paulo. He became Emperor Pedro I.
